recipes.name: Adas bil Hamod (Lebanese Lentil Lemon Soup)
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package frozen whole leaf spinach

steps.text: Heat oil in large pot over high heat. When oil is very hot, add onions and stir until onions begin to turn dark brown and caramelize, about 10 minutes. Put the lentils, garlic, frozen spinach, and mint into the pot. Pour in enough water so that it is about 2 inches deeper than the lentil mixture. Stir well to loosen browned bits of onion on the bottom of the pot.

Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium. Simmer, uncovered, until lentils are tender, about 20 minutes. If soup gets too thick, add a little more water. Salt to taste. Lower heat and stir in lemon juice.

raw_recipe.headline: Adas bil Hamod (Lebanese Lentil Lemon Soup)
raw_recipe.description: This Lebanese version of traditional lentil soup with spinach is seasoned with mint and lemon juice. It's traditionally served with toasted French bread for dipping.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make a Lebanese version of a traditional Middle Eastern lentil soup. Spinach simmers with garlic, lentils, mint, and lemon juice in this very healthy soup. The mint and lemon juice give the soup a distinctive brightness. You’ll love it!

review.reviewBody: This is true to the Lebanese recipe...and yes, you DO have to love lemon to love this, as is! I make this slightly differently. I boil the lentils first and sautee the onions in a separate pan, adding them to the pot once the lentils are near finished. Then, I add the salt, some pepper and the spinach and simmer at medium-low heat until the flavours blend. I personally don't use dried mint in this recipe. My husband would find the original version to be too be "lemony" also, so we only add a small amount to the pot, then add lemon to individual servings, as preferred. Just a thought for an alternate version: you can substitute Swiss Chard for the spinach. My family is split down the middle as to which of these tastes better.

Nice soup. I burned the onions to the pot :( Next time I'll cook the onions in a separate pan. I used 1/2 vegetable stock and 1/2 water. Mostly lemon juice, but also one fresh squeezed lemon. I used 1/2 frozen and half fresh chopped spinach. I think I would just go all frozen next time to make it easier. I think I'll also leave the lid on next time to save the broth from evaporating, and maybe add more broth/water. Don't forget to rinse your lentils.

A fabulous and easy soup ... not to mention that its totally nutritious. Took all of 15 minutes to put together & 35 to low-boil/simmer, covered to save the broth from evaporating. Lentils are amazing little suckers ... peppery, almost smoky, they carry the simplicity of this soup almost on their own. For those that say it was missing taste, try this: Instead of using plain water as a base, start with about 4 cups vegetable broth (or even 3-4 boullion cubes & 4 cups water). Secondly, I had the time to use chopped fresh spinach, and also used fresh lemon juice ... nice touch (certainly wasn't too lemony for a full pot of soup!). Lastly, don't hesitate to season with some Kosher salt (the chunky stuff ... the best for cooking!), and plenty of freshly ground pepper. Bottom line: never use plain water as a soup base ... get some broth, or at least some boullion. You may even try cooking the lentils separately as another reviewer noted, and adjust the broth level as you cook.

I absolutely love this recipe ! I will admit I altered it just a little, I didn't use the fresh mint I did use fresh ginger instead. I also allowed the garlic, ginger, and onions to cook together so to really pick up the flavor prior to me adding the water. I used fresh spinach also, and Kosher Sea Salt at first but opted to using a teaspoon of table salt which did the trick! The lemon juice just made the whole soup complete! Oh and i also sliced up some avocado for garnish :)

Like this recipe. I make a couple of changes. I begin with chicken broth (from a box), saute the onion and garlic separately then add them to the simmering lentils. I use fresh spinach or chard. I cut it up and put it in the soup bowl and pour the hot soup over it as I like fresh greens just barely cooked. I also add more seasoning--garlic powder, seasoned salt, cumin, pepper, a little cayenne. Love the lemony taste, gives it a nice tang.

It’s a homey, simple soup. I made it with vegetable stock, went easy on the lemon, and topped it with some sour cream and cilantro. Delicious and soothing. I’m new to lentils and this is a perfect, clear, staple soup.

When I first made this soup I didn't really like it on the first try. It was pretty bland. After letting it sit for a day and let all the flavors blend together I really liked it. But this is a very basic, rustic, super healthy and vegan soup so keep that in mind. Very very easy to make and cheap too! Definitely use vegetable stock instead of water, make sure to add salt and use fresh lemon juice and fresh spinach. Serve with warm pita bread and it's quite delicious :)

This is a delicious and easy-to-make dish! I followed the tips that other reviewers gave and replaced the water with vegetable stock and used fresh spinach and fresh lemon juice. I put the left overs in the fridge and had it cold the next day, which was very nice as well. Makes it a very nice summer dish!
This soup was good as following the instructions, except I didn't use so much lemon. I cut it back by half. I think next time I will use my emulsifier and make crushed lentil soup.
It was good but flat. If I make it again, I will use more lemon and olive oil and use a hand blender to give it some body.

This was very delicious! I made it exactly as given, except I didn't have any spinach and replaced it with Swiss chard tops and some beet tops. I only had 1 extra large lemon and I thought that was perfect in taste, anymore would have been overpowering. I will make this again!

Good! I didn't use quite as much lemon as called for and I did add cayenne and cumin...saw those in a different but similar recipe. I don't think those additions changed much. Flavorful soup and good recipe. I already had black lentils cooked so very fast to make. I added in Greek yogurt to my serving but others didn't and liked the soup plenty.
I simply love Lebanese food! It's so delicious and flavourful. I love how varied it can be.
I really enjoyed this. I also used red lentils instead, but that's only a personal preference. Thanks for the recipe!
awesome !
it was o.k not the best
We thought it was fabulous.
Excellent flavor. Easy to make. I used fresh mint.
The more lemon, the better!

I made this as written, except I used fresh spinach. I also just made half a recipe. It just wasn’t flavorful enough for me, even with the lemon. If I try it again, I’d use more mint, perhaps fresh instead of dry.
